about: The MCP requests that HostLab sends to its dexsql backend and what it reads from the answers, taken from the frozen HostLab source (conformance/corpus/hostlab/source-8782f43/analysis_batch.py). check_hostlab_required_tools.py puts exactly these requests to the server and checks that every argument is in the published schema and every field HostLab reads is in the answer. A field that HostLab reads is a promise; one that it does not read may differ (see the declared differences of conformance/decode/a0_replay.py).

calls.note: has_dex false makes HostLab refuse the input; diagnostics are passed on as source_diagnostics

sql: SELECT file_id,entry_name FROM dex_files ORDER BY file_id

calls.note: builds the file_id -> DEX entry map; a partial answer is an error for HostLab

sql: SELECT file_id,descriptor FROM methods ORDER BY file_id,method_idx

calls.note: HostLab joins pages until next_offset is null or 64000 bytes are reached
the continuation must make progress (next_offset above the offset) and end with null; the joined pages equal the one page of max_lines 1000
HostLab keeps the answer as the manifest section of its report and marks it partial when next_offset is not null

errors_read.meaning: the dataset is gone; the batch stops using it
a rejected read-only statement does not invalidate the dataset

discovery.tools_list: the eight registered tools carry the reference's published schemas (run_mcp_conformance.py: schemas)
discovery.why: MDD-072; a tool that is not implemented is not listed

not_called_note: find_refs and apk_info belong to HostLab's sqlite backend and are not part of the native MCP surface
